item.title: Stripping extra dependencies in .NET NativeAOT apps using linker substitutions
item.description: In this post I describe how to perform method-substitutions with the NativeAOT linker to remove additional dependencies that the linker couldn't see were unused Worth a read for developers following .NET. Link to article: https://andrewlock.net/stripping-extra-dependencies-in-.net-nativeaot-apps-using-linker-substitutions

item.title: Designing APIs for AI agents: your API has a new user
item.description: AI agents are a new kind of API consumer: they call endpoints, retry requests, and chain multi-step workflows on their own. This post covers practical ASP.NET Core patterns for building agent-ready APIs, including DTOs, idempotency, pagination, machine-readable errors, auth, and llms.txt. Worth a read for developers following AI and .NET. Link to article: https://blog.elmah.io/designing-apis-for-ai-agents-your-api-has-a-new-user

item.title: Introducing GLM 5.3 on Amazon Bedrock
item.description: GLM 5.3 from Z.ai is now available on Amazon Bedrock: a 753B-parameter mixture-of-experts model built for coding and long-horizon agentic tasks. Learn how to invoke it with the OpenAI-compatible APIs, cut cost and latency with prompt caching, and run an authorized security test with the open-source Strix agent. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/introducing-glm-5-3-on-amazon-bedrock

item.title: Generate unit tests for your modernized code with AWS Transform for .NET
item.description: When you modernize a .NET Framework application to modern .NET, you end up with a transformed, buildable codebase — but the question that immediately follows is always the same: how do I safely keep changing it from here? Once the code is modernized, your team keeps evolving it — fixing bugs, adding features, upgrading dependencies […] Worth a read for developers following .NET and AWS. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/dotnet/generate-unit-tests-for-your-modernized-code-with-aws-transform-for-net

item.title: Supercharge regulated workloads with Claude Code and Amazon Bedrock
item.description: Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 are available on Amazon Bedrock in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. Learn how to use them with Claude Code, Anthropic's agentic coding tool, for compliance-aligned, AI-assisted development on regulated and ITAR workloads. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/supercharge-regulated-workloads-with-claude-code-and-amazon-bedrock

item.title: New agent skill: Amazon SageMaker optimized generative AI inference for your coding agent
item.description: Amazon SageMaker optimized generative AI inference introduces the aws-ai-ml skill through the Agent Toolkit for AWS, giving coding agents like Kiro, Claude Code, and Codex deep expertise in inference optimization and benchmarking. Describe what you want, and your agent generates executable SageMaker Python SDK v3 code to benchmark, recommend, and compare deployments. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/new-agent-skill-amazon-sagemaker-optimized-generative-ai-inference-for-your-coding-agent

item.title: UWP and WinUI 3 apps: UI testing with MSTest
item.description: Learn how to test UWP and WinUI 3 apps with MSTest and Microsoft.Testing.Platform across packaged, unpackaged, and AppContainer hosts. The post UWP and WinUI 3 apps: UI testing with MSTest appeared first on .NET Blog . Worth a read for developers following Testing and .NET. Link to article: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/testing-uwp-and-winui-3-apps-with-mstest

item.title: Making Amazon Quick enterprise-ready: Automated, auditable cross-account resource promotion
item.description: Promoting Amazon Quick resources (agents, action connectors, knowledge bases, flows, and spaces) from a development to a production AWS account has been a manual, error-prone chore. This post shows how to automate cross-account promotion with an idempotent, auditable MCP server on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/making-amazon-quick-enterprise-ready-automated-auditable-cross-account-resource-promotion

item.title: Agentic retrieval with LangChain and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
item.description: Build a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) application on Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base with LangChain, and see how agentic retrieval handles the multi-part questions that single-shot retrieval answers poorly. Run the same query through both paths, read the trace events, and compare what each retrieval path costs. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/agentic-retrieval-with-langchain-and-amazon-bedrock-knowledge-bases

item.title: Downgrading user roles in Amazon Quick
item.description: Amazon Quick doesn't offer a direct console path to downgrade a user from Admin or Author to Reader. This post walks through two reliable methods: a manual delete-and-recreate approach and an AWS CLI step-down sequence that downgrades roles safely while preserving asset ownership. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/downgrading-user-roles-in-amazon-quick

item.title: Evaluating multi-agent systems for explainability and helpfulness with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description: Multi-agent systems need deeper guarantees than fluent responses: they must select the right tools, respect constraints, and explain their decisions. Learn how to build a Strands-based multi-agent supply chain decisioning system and evaluate it with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations using built-in, custom, and explainability evaluators. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/evaluating-multi-agent-systems-for-explainability-and-helpfulness-with-amazon-bedrock-agentcore

item.title: Our approach to EU text provenance rules
item.description: How OpenAI is approaching text watermarking under EU rules. Learn where watermarks apply, how detection works, and why access starts with researchers. Worth a read for developers following AI. Link to article: https://openai.com/index/eu-text-provenance

item.title: Code Quality: Designing Method Parameters in .NET
item.description: When writing .NET code, use descriptive camelCase parameter names that convey their purpose instead of data types, avoiding Hungarian notation. Validate arguments in public methods and employ enums for clarity when using Boolean parameters. These practices enhance code readability, maintainability, and overall quality. Worth a read for developers following .NET. Link to article: https://dotnettips.com/2026/10/04/code-quality-designing-method-parameters-in-net

item.title: Sweep thousands of leases for compliance using Amazon Quick and the Adjudicated Query pattern
item.description: The Adjudicated Query pattern pairs the Amazon Quick chat agent with a bounded MCP server over a deterministic rules engine to deliver provably complete, defensible compliance answers. This post walks through the reference architecture and a deployable AWS CDK sample, using lease compliance as the running example. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. item.title: Add secure Web Search to Claude Desktop with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description: Claude Desktop on Amazon Bedrock is limited to the model's knowledge cutoff without web search. In this post, we walk through connecting Claude Desktop to Web Search using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, with JWT-based inbound authentication through AWS IAM Identity Center and Amazon Cognito. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/add-secure-web-search-to-claude-desktop-with-amazon-bedrock-agentcore

item.title: Fine-tune a search agent with multi-turn RL on Amazon SageMaker AI
item.description: Fine-tuning teaches a small search agent your tools and environment, giving it the reliability of a frontier model at lower latency and cost. In this post, we fine-tune an LLM-powered search agent with multi-turn reinforcement learning (MTRL) on Amazon SageMaker AI and share the gains we measured in retrieval quality and reliability. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/fine-tune-a-search-agent-with-multi-turn-rl-on-amazon-sagemaker-ai

The gist of it is that larger redesigns in established code bases rarely happen because changing too much code in one go risks conflicting with parallel work being done by colleagues. item.title: Back to Basics: CSS @container Filtering
item.description: While viewport-based @media queries are a staple of responsive web design, they fall short in dynamic or resizable multi-pane layouts. The newish CSS @container at-rule solves this by allowing styles to adapt based on the size of a specific parent container rather than the entire browser window. In this post, explore the differences between @media and @container, and describe how you can quickly move queries… Worth a read for developers following Containers.

item.description: Chatham Financial uses Codex and GPT-5.6 to build technology and redesign workflows, cutting trade validation from 30 minutes to under 4. Worth a read for developers following AI. Link to article: https://openai.com/index/chatham-financial

item.title: Scaling cloud migrations with agentic AI on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description: Learn how AWS Professional Services uses a multi-agent framework built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to automate enterprise cloud migrations end to end. Purpose-built AI agents handle discovery, infrastructure as code generation, portfolio governance, and post-migration operations, reducing IaC development time from weeks to minutes. item.title: Serve live, governed data in AI-built apps with Amazon Quick
item.description: With Live Data in Apps in Amazon Quick, AI-built apps query your governed Quick Sight datasets in real time instead of static, build-time snapshots. Each query runs as the person viewing the app, so row-level and column-level security apply per reader. Learn how to build, publish, and share a live-data app using natural language. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/serve-live-governed-data-in-ai-built-apps-with-amazon-quick

item.title: Build agent memory with NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit and Amazon S3 Vectors
item.description: Learn how to use Amazon S3 Vectors as the persistent memory layer within the NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit (NAT), deployed on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). This post shows how NAT's memory subsystem works and how to implement Amazon S3 Vectors as a custom memory provider, using a multi-agent investment research use case. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/build-agent-memory-with-nvidia-nemo-agent-toolkit-and-amazon-s3-vectors

item.title: The eternal complement

item.title: Uplifting conversion across the acquisition funnel with personalization using contextual bandits on AWS
item.description: Generative AI makes it cheap to produce personalized content at scale, but which variation do you show each customer? Amazon Payments used a multi-objective contextual bandit on Amazon SageMaker AI to personalize an acquisition funnel, achieving a high single-digit conversion lift for one audience, and learning why content, not the model, was the constraint. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/uplifting-conversion-across-the-acquisition-funnel-with-personalization-using-contextual-bandits-on-aws

item.title: Building ambient agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: From event-driven signals to human-in-the-loop workflows
item.description: Ambient agents respond to events such as an Amazon S3 upload, a schedule, or an alert instead of waiting for a chat prompt. This post walks through building framework-agnostic ambient agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore using Amazon SQS, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB, with a single ask_human tool and a Jobs page for human-in-the-loop review. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI.
